headline: IonQ announced that it has set up Romania's national quantum-secure communications network, one of the largest in Europe.
score_reason: Pool score 5 lowered by 2: the announcement dates from 26 Feb 2026 and the page was re-dated; the figures are IonQ's own and nothing independent is reported.
importance_line: A national network of quantum-protected links is said to be running in Romania, which would give government, health and research users a way to protect sensitive data, but the scale and the benefit are IonQ's own claims and the news is from February.
summary: Stocktwits reports that IonQ, a US quantum computing company, said it built Romania's national quantum key distribution network, a system that uses quantum physics to share secret encryption keys, together with a Bucharest technical university and Romania's research and education network. IonQ says the network spans more than 1,500 kilometres, about a fifth of Europe's land-based quantum communication links, and is among the largest outside China; the announcement dates from 26 Feb 2026, so this is older news.
notes: Older news re-dated (feed date 11 Oct 2026; event 26 Feb 2026, dated from Google News listings of IonQ's release and other outlets, not from the article text). Read Stocktwits in full (HTTP 200). I did not read IonQ's own release; the credit goes to Stocktwits, which wrote its own market-flavoured piece, and IonQ is named inside. The share-price and earnings parts were left out as market chatter.
